execution_overview.overall_summary: Rewrote and fixed Python scripts to faithfully execute both tasks. Task1 now computes the Spearman correlation between openness_average and participation coefficient and a median-split Welch t-test, both significant. Task2 compares gender groups '0' vs '1' with 90% node retention and reports non-significant differences with group sizes and exclusions.

deviations.description: Fixed filtering and sample construction; ensured non-missing part_mean and openness_average; removed unnecessary merges; added explicit n reporting and saved filtered dataset for verification.
deviations.reason: Original attempt produced null results due to a logic/scoping bug that incorrectly yielded an empty correlation sample.

method_fidelity.fidelity_note: The analysis followed the planned path: built the global entropy matrix, constructed per-participant networks, computed metrics (CPL, betweenness, participation), applied cpl < 10, then ran Spearman correlation and median-split Welch t-test.

result_raw.result_text: Spearman correlation between openness_average and participation coefficient (part_mean) is rho=0.160, p=0.000265 (n=516). Median-split Welch t-test shows higher part_mean in the higher-openness group (t=-2.947, p=0.00336; n_low=258, n_high=258).

conclusion.conclusion_text: Higher openness is associated with higher participation coefficient in the semantic networks, supporting the focal association as planned.

deviations.description: Excluded blank/whitespace gender values; explicitly compared gender groups '0' vs '1'; reported group sizes and count excluded.
deviations.reason: Original result compared an unintended blank-coded group. Adjustment ensures a faithful gender comparison while respecting the dataset coding.

method_fidelity.fidelity_note: Kept 90% nodes by removing top 10% eigenvector-centrality nodes, computed metrics, applied cpl < 10 and valid gender filter, and conducted a Welch t-test comparing '0' vs '1'.

result_raw.result_text: Welch t-test on participation coefficient by gender (0 vs 1) after 90% node retention: t=0.877, p=0.382 (n0=103, n1=398; 15 excluded due to blank/nonbinary coding).

conclusion.conclusion_text: This comparable analysis tests gender differences, not the focal openness association; the non-significant difference does not inform the focal claim.
